option_assessments.label: A
option_assessments.assessment: False as written: let itself runs on its receiver even when null; only ?.let skips the block. Covers let, but not Elvis, so incomplete for the compound question.

option_assessments.label: B
option_assessments.assessment: False: ?: supplies the right-hand fallback for null and can also throw/return; says nothing about let, so incomplete.

option_assessments.label: C
option_assessments.assessment: Best/keyed answer, but the let clause is overgeneralized: plain let does not filter null; ?.let does. The shown option omits ?. and therefore is not fully correct under the literal reading.

option_assessments.label: D
option_assessments.assessment: False: Elvis returns the non-null left operand, otherwise the right; omits let and so is incomplete.

axes.SEMANTICS: FAIL: C is not literally correct because let alone runs for nullable receiver; A also ambiguously describes let but is false as written.
axes.ANSC: FAIL: every wrong omits one of the two requested concepts; C covers both only if “let” is taken as shorthand for ?.let, an unstated condition.
axes.SFPL: FAIL: C is the only option covering both Elvis and let; the three wrongs are single-mechanism and much less complete.
axes.RU: PASS: wording is generally understandable; “тип-вопрос” not relevant here; “как раз” in D mildly colloquial but clear.
axes.FACTS: Verified against official Kotlin API and docs: let passes receiver as argument and returns lambda result; null gating comes from ?. ; Elvis evaluates RHS when LHS is null.
axes.SECTIONS: FAIL: several wrong explanation fields discuss only one member of the compound question; A.how_it_should_be incorrectly credits let with ?. behavior.
axes.LINKAGE: Q6 theory directly distinguishes let from ?.let and explains Elvis; visible question omits ?. qualifier, leaving key/choice wording imprecise.

current_theory: Theory explicitly states ordinary let does not check null and ?.let skips block; Elvis fallback applies when the entire left expression is null, including a null let result. This contradicts literal option C wording that let itself executes only for non-null.
